name: Caiaphas
title: The High Priest Who Condemned Jesus
summary: Caiaphas (Joseph son of Caiaphas) was the high priest in Jerusalem from about 18 to 36 AD. He played a central role in the trial of Jesus and declared that it was better for one man to die than for the whole nation to perish. He was also involved in the persecution of the early church.

keyEvents.title: Council to Put Jesus to Death
keyEvents.description: Caiaphas prophesied without knowing that Jesus would die for the people, and from that day on they made plans to kill Jesus.

keyEvents.title: The Trial of Jesus Before the Jewish Council
keyEvents.description: Caiaphas led the trial of Jesus in his home and tore his clothes when Jesus confessed that he was the Messiah, the Son of God, declaring it blasphemy.

keyEvents.title: Jesus is sent to Pilate
keyEvents.description: After the council had found Jesus guilty, they brought him to the Roman governor Pontius Pilate to have a death sentence carried out.

keyEvents.title: Caiaphas' father-in-law Annas interrogates Jesus
keyEvents.description: Jesus was first brought to Annas, who was Caiaphas' father-in-law and former high priest, before being sent on to Caiaphas.

keyEvents.title: Persecution of the apostles
keyEvents.description: Caiaphas was present when Peter and John were brought before the Jewish council after healing a lame man at the temple, and he tried to stop preaching in Jesus' name.

keyEvents.title: The apostles are imprisoned and interrogated again
keyEvents.description: The high priest and his supporters imprisoned the apostles out of jealousy, but an angel freed them. They were still brought before the council again.
